item.title: What is Loop Transformer and how GLM-5.4 is catching up to 2-3 trillion parameter models
item.description:
How to make neural networks smarter without inflating them to gigantic sizes? The answer was presented on November 23 by the Chinese laboratory Z.ai, previously known as Zhipu AI. 28 layers, two passes, and not a single new parameter. This is how the new GLM is structured, according to TNW. GLM-5.4 has become the company's first flagship model based on the Loop Transformer architecture, where the same layers are applied to a token repeatedly. What this is and how it affects model inference is discussed below. Read more

item.title: I tried to figure out how and why Claude bans users
item.description:
In November 2026, a wave of bans and verification requests (read: bans) swept through Claude users. People started losing their paid accounts mid-work, with even those using their own VPS and paying with personal foreign cards falling under the blocks. To understand which combinations still work and what almost certainly leads to a ban, I surveyed nearly 300 subscribers to my channel. Among them, 189 people have already lost their accounts, and 108 continue to work. Below is what's really happening with the blocks, what actions trigger them, and how not to lose your work data. item.title: Brand Visibility in Neural Networks: Why Auditing Yandex Alice AI and ChatGPT Requires Customer Queries
item.description:
Recommendations for auditing brand visibility in neural networks depend on how well the test questions align with actual customer queries. If SEO keywords describe a different task, an analyst risks recommending website improvements or content placement that doesn't help the customer make a choice. Since June 2026, I've been measuring brand visibility in neural networks, conducting 39 measurements by the end of August. My logs show that reducing the number of questions impacts accuracy more than reducing the number of services tested. To check SEO keywords, two comparable sets are needed: real customer queries and questions from search keywords. Comparisons should be made for answers about the same anonymized brand in the same niche, separately for Yandex Alice AI and ChatGPT. The origin of the phrasing should be changed while preserving the user's task. Read more

item.title: Harness and AI Review: How Modern AI Agents Review Your Code
item.description:
For years, code review was a bottleneck where teams spent more time than on feature creation. But now, code review has become the bottleneck. Thanks to the widespread adoption of AI agents, code is being created very quickly, perhaps too quickly. According to 2026 Faros telemetry (22,000 developers), teams with high AI agent adoption saw their average pull request size increase by 51%. Coupled with this growth, the number of bugs per developer increased by 54%. The PR itself becomes the bottleneck; they can linger for days in your company or open-source project, context can be lost, and evaluation time is spent, sometimes in vain. Review is an important part of finding bugs that tests or developers couldn't catch, or deviations from code style, violations of clean code, and so on. A human could review, but unfortunately, they aren't always capable of handling even a regular large PR, and when the quantity and size increase, it becomes simply difficult. In this article, I'll discuss how to help your corporate or open-source project if it's drowning in code reviews, and I'll cover existing solutions like Devin AI, Context7, DeepWiki, Rabbit Code Review, and others. Read more

item.title: Artificial Intelligence is the New Digital "Drone"
item.description:
First, about what AI is now. Models are getting smarter with each generation, and we are promised that in the near future they will become a "digital god," a new industrial revolution, etc. We are being "sold" something that should be obvious to everyone. But the facts say otherwise. Open models can already be put on hardware assembled in a garage for $30-50k and directed at any target. And this is already happening: in July 2026, a swarm of about 700 AI agents hacked Hugging Face's infrastructure and tried to cover their tracks. This is the first confirmed case of a cyberattack being carried out entirely by an autonomous AI. Wikipedia · MIT Technology Review: why the agents did it · OpenAI Report · Reuters Hacked supermarket refrigerators in Europe, shutdown of all flights in the US on November 13. AI involvement is not officially confirmed, only suspected. Wikipedia: 2026 European refrigerator hacks · Guardian · Wikipedia: 2026 FAA nationwide ground stop · The Atlantic: Americans blamed AI. This gap between promises and practice is the context without which it is difficult to understand the main idea of the article. Large language models are dangerous now and will become even more dangerous in the near future. Why do I think so? I haven't seen a comparison of large language models with drones in the mainstream, and I think it will be useful for everyone to look at working with neural networks from this angle. There is a principle in science: believe your eyes. And today, my eyes see the following. Read more

item.description:

item.title: The number of articles per year is growing, but there is no progress
item.description:
Globally, up to 3.5 million scientific papers are published annually, registered in international databases like Scopus. This excludes national journals not indexed internationally but searchable. China alone contributes about 1 million articles yearly. In 2010, the global output was around 2 million articles per year. Over the last 15 years, scientific content production has increased by over 65%. Even in specialized fields like neurobiology, up to 100,000 articles are published annually. Reading all of them daily would require 137 hours, assuming 30 minutes per article. Consequently, up to 80% of articles in humanities and social sciences remain uncited. Read more
